one_line: Mughal emperor Humayun, caught in Sher Shah Suri’s monsoon ambush at Chausa in 1539, struggling to hold his camp and escape the rising Ganges.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s, tall and slightly lean with a scholar-warrior build rather than purely muscular.
appearance.face: Oval face, light brown Central Asian–Indian complexion, finely arched brows, slightly downturned thoughtful eyes with dark lashes, straight medium nose, trimmed moustache and short pointed beard; default expression is calm but worried, eyes scanning as if calculating options even under pressure.
appearance.hair: Shoulder-length straight black hair, neatly combed back from the forehead, mostly hidden under a dark emerald green turban wound in Central Asian-Mughal style with a modest gold band and a single small white heron feather tucked on the left side.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate mid-16th-century Mughal camp attire: a long quilted jamma (overlapping wrap coat) in deep teal silk, calf-length, fastening right to left with small gold buttons, subtly patterned with fine diagonal stitching suggesting light padding for travel; beneath it, glimpses of a cream-coloured cotton tunic; a wide maroon silk patka (waist sash) wrapped twice around the waist and knotted on the left with its embroidered ends hanging to mid-thigh, decorated with narrow gold floral borders; loose, slightly tapered off-white cotton paijama trousers; soft mid-calf leather riding boots in dark brown with simple stitched panels, slightly worn from use; over his shoulders a thin, waterproofed dark indigo wool chadar (cloak) thrown back but ready to pull up against rain, its edge lined with a narrow gold and red border; minimal jewellery—a small gold signet ring on his right hand and a simple jade bead bracelet on his left wrist—conveying royalty without ostentation in the chaos of a flooded camp.
appearance.signature: A sheathed, slightly curved Indo-Turkic sabre (talwar) with a steel hilt and disc pommel, suspended at his left hip from a brown leather belt concealed under the maroon patka, the scabbard wrapped in dark red leather with a narrow brass throat and chape; in tense moments his right hand rests on the hilt, emphasizing both imperial authority and readiness as he navigates the monsoon-night ambush.

ref_desc: Humayun is a late-30s tall, lean Mughal emperor with light brown complexion, trimmed moustache and pointed beard, wearing a dark emerald green turban with a white feather, a deep teal quilted jamma over cream tunic and off-white paijama, maroon patka, dark brown riding boots, and a dark red-sheathed talwar at his left hip accented by gold details.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Humayun at Chausa: a late-30s tall, slightly lean Mughal emperor with light brown complexion, oval face, thoughtful downturned eyes, straight nose, trimmed moustache and short pointed beard, default expression calm but worried; shoulder-length straight black hair mostly hidden under a dark emerald green Central Asian–Mughal turban, banded with a modest gold strip and a single small white feather on the left side. Dress him in a deep teal silk quilted jamma, calf-length, overlapping right to left with fine diagonal stitching and small gold buttons, worn over a cream cotton tunic visible at the collar and cuffs. At his waist tie a wide maroon silk patka wrapped twice and knotted on the left, its ends hanging to mid-thigh with narrow gold floral embroidery; give him loose off-white cotton paijama and soft mid-calf dark brown leather riding boots with simple stitched panels. Add a thin dark indigo wool chadar with a narrow red-and-gold border draped around his shoulders, mostly pushed back. Keep jewellery minimal: a small gold signet ring on his right hand and a jade bead bracelet on his left wrist. At his left hip, suspend a slightly curved talwar in a dark red leather scabbard with brass fittings from a belt hidden under the patka; pose him so his right hand rests lightly on the hilt, the colours dominated by deep teal, emerald green, maroon, cream and dark brown, ready to be reused consistently in many panels.
